hypothesis: A deny-by-default inherited environment, invocation-scoped home, per-harness authentication projection, explicit native readable roots, and an OS-enforced provider-only egress proxy prevent daemon and operator authentication material from crossing into native agent tools without breaking required CLI login or workspace execution.
sourceRefs: security-review finding for native CLI host authority inheritance

metricsCompared.name: unrelated daemon credential variables available to native children
metricsCompared.baseline: full daemon environment inherited; Codex removed only the OpenAI key variable
metricsCompared.candidate: 0 of the asserted unrelated provider, GitHub, notification, and cloud authentication material present across all three native harnesses

metricsCompared.name: native host filesystem visibility
metricsCompared.baseline: macOS allowed default reads and Linux mounted the complete host root read-only
metricsCompared.candidate: macOS emits a default read denial with explicit roots; Linux constructs an empty namespace without mounting host root

metricsCompared.name: native child network reachability
metricsCompared.baseline: macOS allowed all outbound networking and Linux retained the host network namespace
metricsCompared.candidate: macOS permits only the run-local CONNECT proxy; Linux unshares networking and bridges only that proxy over a mounted Unix socket; unlisted hosts and direct loopback bypasses are denied

metricsCompared.name: focused harness and boundary regressions
metricsCompared.baseline: no cross-harness secret inheritance, host-read isolation, or mediated-egress regressions
metricsCompared.candidate: 64/64 focused security, harness, auth-projection, egress, layout, module-boundary, and strict-type tests passing

rationale: This closes a confirmed high-severity disclosure path at the shared native-child and OS-sandbox boundaries. Exact harness auth remains available through copied Codex/Gemini login state or Antigravity's OS keyring, provider calls traverse an explicit hostname allowlist while native tools have no direct route, explicit workflow runtime additions remain supported, and focused security/protocol tests plus type, format, and task validation pass.
